title: Simultaneous K-flat telescope resolutions for an exact evaluation functor
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to its module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $W$ an object, and $A=\mathcal O(W)$. Suppose evaluation $E:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exact, preserves all small colimits, and sends every flat sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] to a flat $A$-module. For every unbounded cochain complex $K$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] there exist bounded-above termwise-flat complexes $E_n$, transitions $t_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ and termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphisms $q_n:E_n\to\tau_{\le n}K$, $n\in\mathbf N$, strictly compatible after the good truncation inclusions $\iota_n:\tau_{\le n}K\to K$. Put $B=\bigoplus_n E_n$ and $P=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $s$ induced by the transitions into the next summand. The map $p:P\to K$ with unshifted component $\sum_n q_n\iota_n$ and shifted component zero is a chain map and a quasi-isomorphism. In fact the canonical map $P\to\operatorname{colim}_nE_n$ and the induced map $\operatorname{colim}_nE_n\to\operatorname{colim}_n\tau_{\le n}K=K$ are quasi-isomorphisms; the last equality holds degree by degree. The terms of $P$ are flat and $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Evaluation identifies $E(P)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(1-E(s):\bigoplus_n E(E_n)\to\bigoplus_n E(E_n))$ as complexes. Each $E(E_n)$ is bounded above with flat $A$-module terms, so this evaluated telescope is K-flat over $A$ (view modules as sheaves on the one-object site with trivial topology). Also $E(p):E(P)\to E(K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. No functorial choice of the tower and no preservation of all K-flat complexes by $E$ is asserted.

proof.text: Use the independent-universe functorial flat-cover datum [lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution]. Reduce its left resolution to preserve zero morphisms. Apply the bounded-above totalization functor to all bounded-above complexes at once. Its augmentation is quasi-isomorphic and its terms are flat; it is termwise epic because the summand in bidegree (i,0) maps onto the original degree-i term. The composite of this inclusion with the augmentation is the flat cover, preceded by the degree-zero resolution isomorphism. Take its composition with the good truncation diagram indexed by natural numbers. Naturality gives strict compatibility, including at n=0. Transport categorical flatness through the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. All these constructions are performed at the independent universes of the statement, without applying the single-universe flat-truncation-tower interface.

source.place: Tag 077J; bounded-above resolution construction, using FromJoel LeftResolution.CochainComplexMinus

proof.text: Construct B as the countable coproduct of the stages, and u by its legs j_n-t_n j_(n+1). For each finite subcoproduct, a retraction of its composite with u is the sum of the projections onto a stage j given on stage k by the transition k→j for k≤j and zero otherwise. Consecutive terms cancel. Thus u is monic by exactness of the filtered colimit of finite subcoproducts. The map a from B to colim D is the sum of the colimit injections and satisfies ua=0. A cofork of u gives compatible legs of a D-cocone by induction on the natural-number interval; this explicitly proves that a is a cokernel. Hence (u,a) is short exact. The canonical mapping-cone map r to its cokernel is a quasi-isomorphism, and the cone desc equations give its prescribed unshifted component and zero shifted component. This proves the general categorical telescope comparison inline, rather than invoking the single-universe sheaf specialization.

Let T be the good truncation diagram and α the natural augmentation of the resolution functor on T. Its canonical cocone ι into K is colimiting in every degree: after n=i.toNat+1 every truncation inclusion in degree i is an isomorphism. The eventually constant colimit criterion and HomologicalComplex.isColimitOfEval give this cocone its colimit structure. Let g:colim T≅K be the uniquely normalized colimit isomorphism. Filtered colimits of module sheaves are exact, by the exactness-reflecting forgetful functor to abelian sheaves and exact filtered colimits of abelian groups. Thus the Mathlib colimMap criterion makes colim α a quasi-isomorphism. Define b=(colim α)g and p=rb. The colimit and cone equations give all normalized component formulas and p has zero shifted component. Composition of quasi-isomorphisms gives quasi-isomorphy of b and p.

source.place: Tag 077J, final assertion and proof; good truncations and exact filtered colimits

proof.text: Tensor preserves small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. Flat objects are therefore closed under the required coproducts, since exact coproducts of exact tensor functors are exact, and under binary biproducts. Evaluating the coproduct cocone degree by degree and using the cone term isomorphism proves termwise flatness of the telescope. The stages are K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat]. Tensoring an acyclic complex with the coproduct remains acyclic: use the functor-category short-complex equivalence and exactness of coproducts. Tensor commutes with the cone by [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso]; its two inputs are acyclic, so the cone is acyclic by the distinguished triangle. This proves the required independent-coefficient K-flatness.

Set BA=E(B), jA=E(j), tA=E(t), and uA=E(u), with c the identity. Preservation of coproducts makes the evaluated cocone colimiting, and additivity gives its displayed shift identity. Use Mathlib mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso for eP. Its map_inr equation gives the unshifted normalization; the explicit comparison matrix and the inl-fst and inl-snd identities give the shifted normalization. Evaluation preserves zero objects, so every evaluated stage is bounded above; the given flat-to-flat hypothesis gives flat terms. For ordinary modules the bounded-above categorical K-flat criterion follows from module flatness, exact filtered colimits and the total tensor API. Apply the same exact-coproduct and tensor-cone arguments to obtain acyclic total tensors for the evaluated telescope.

source.place: Tags 06YQ and 07A3; explicit additive cone comparison

proof.text: Evaluation preserves finite limits by the module-sheaf evaluation instance and finite colimits by hypothesis. Apply the exact-functor homology comparison [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], in its Mathlib quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology form, to p. This gives QuasiIso E(p); no preservation of arbitrary K-flat complexes is used.

Step 1: lem-pc-flat-truncation-tower gives the tower and the compatibility a_{n+1}t_n=a_n. Step 2: recomputed by hand; with u=1-s, au=0, d_P^2=0, and p(b,c)=a(b) is a chain map in the cone convention of def-weil-abstract-derived-category (target summand B^i). Step 3: the canonical cone-to-colimit map r(b,c)=pi(b), with p=b∘r (lem-pc-complex-hocolim-colimit, Tag 0949). Step 4: monicity of iota_{n+1} makes (q_n) a map of sequences; the filtered-colimit clause of lem-pc-kflat-hocolim-truncations applies; (tau<=n K)^i=K^i for n>=max(0,i+1), so the colimit is K degreewise. Step 5: lem-pc-kflat-closure gives K-flatness of B and P and flatness of the countable sums B^i ⊕ B^{i+1}. Step 6: evaluation preserves the sum and the cone matrix, so E(P)≅Cone(1-E(s)); K-flatness then follows from the closure node on the one-object site with ring A, where module sheaves and tensor are ordinary A-module ones. Step 7: clause (c) of lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology. All four hypotheses on E are used. Edge cases checked: K=0, a complex in one negative degree, non-injective t_n, A=0, identity evaluation. Sources read: HRS Lemma 4.1(1) and proof; Stacks 077J, 06YS, 06YQ, 06YR, 07A3, 0949, 010N.
